STATISTICS/METRICS\n\n#### HTTP Filter Stats (ext_authz/http)\nThe HTTP ext_authz filter exports the following counters via the `ExtAuthzFilterStats` struct:\n\n**Counter Stats:**\n- `ok` - Number of successful authorization checks\n- `denied` - Number of denied authorization requests\n- `error` - Number of authorization service errors\n- `disabled` - Number of requests where the filter was disabled\n- `failure_mode_allowed` - Number of errors that were allowed due to failure_mode_allow configuration\n- `invalid` - Number of invalid/malformed authorization responses\n- `ignored_dynamic_metadata` - Number of times dynamic metadata injection was ignored (when dynamic metadata ingestion is disabled)\n- `filter_state_name_collision` - Number of times there was a collision when storing logging info in filter state\n\n**Stat Prefix:**\n- Configured via `stat_prefix` config parameter\n- Format: `ext_authz.<stat_prefix>.<stat_name>` (e.g., `ext_authz.waf.ok` or `ext_authz.ok`)\n- Also generates cluster-scoped stats: `ext_authz_ok_`, `ext_authz_denied_`, `ext_authz_error_`, `ext_authz_invalid_`, `ext_authz_failure_mode_allowed_`\n\n#### Network Filter Stats (ext_authz/network)\nThe network ext_authz filter exports both counters and gauges:\n\n**Counter Stats:**\n- `cx_closed` - Number of connections closed due to authorization failure\n- `denied` - Number of denied connections\n- `error` - Number of authorization service errors\n- `failure_mode_allowed` - Number of errors allowed due to failure_mode_allow\n- `ok` - Number of successful checks\n- `total` - Total number of authorization checks\n- `disabled` - Number of connections where filter was disabled\n\n**Gauge Stats:**\n- `active` - Current number of in-flight authorization checks (Accumulate mode)\n\n**Stat Prefix:**\n- Format: `ext_authz.<stat_prefix>.<stat_name>`\n\n---\n\n### 2. Purpose\n\nThe ext_authz filter is an external authorization filter for Envoy proxy that delegates authorization decisions to an external service. Rather than embedding authorization logic directly in Envoy, it sends check requests to a separate authorization server and acts on the response (allow, deny, or error).\n\n**What problems does it solve?**\n\n- **Centralized authorization**: Decouples authorization logic from the proxy, allowing a single authorization service to enforce policies across an entire fleet of Envoy proxies.\n- **Fine-grained access control**: The authorization service receives rich request context (headers, path, client certificate, peer info, request body) and can make nuanced authorization decisions.\n- **Dynamic policy updates**: Authorization policies can be updated in the external service without redeploying Envoy.\n- **Protocol flexibility**: Supports both gRPC and HTTP protocols for communicating with the authorization service, enabling integration with a wide variety of auth backends (OPA, custom services, cloud IAM, etc.).\n\n**When would someone use it?**\n\n- Enforcing authentication/authorization at the edge or service mesh layer.\n- Implementing zero-trust networking where every request must be explicitly authorized.\n- Integrating with external policy engines (e.g., Open Policy Agent).\n- Adding authorization to services that lack their own auth implementation.\n\nThe filter operates at two layers:\n- **HTTP filter** (`envoy.filters.http.ext_authz`): Operates on HTTP requests with full access to headers, path, method, body, and can mutate request/response headers and query parameters based on the authorization response.\n- **Network filter** (`envoy.filters.network.ext_authz`): Operates at the TCP connection level, authorizing connections based on network attributes (source/destination addresses, TLS info) before any HTTP processing.\n\n## 2. Uses Envoy's typed async gRPC client to send `CheckRequest` messages to the `envoy.service.auth.v3.Authorization` service.\n- **source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz/ext_authz_grpc_impl.cc**: gRPC client implementation. Builds and sends CheckRequest, parses CheckResponse on `onSuccess()` (extracting header mutations, query parameter changes, dynamic metadata), handles `onFailure()` for gRPC errors. Helper functions for copying response mutations (`copyHeaderMutations`, `copyQueryParameterMutations`).\n- **source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz/ext_authz_http_impl.h**: `RawHttpClientImpl` class implementing the HTTP authorization client, and `ClientConfig` for HTTP-specific configuration (allowed headers, path prefix, matchers).\n- **source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz/ext_authz_http_impl.cc**: HTTP client implementation. Constructs HTTP requests to the authz service, sends via async HTTP client, parses responses in `toResponse()` (200 = OK, 5xx = Error, anything else = Denied), applies header matchers, extracts dynamic metadata from response headers.\n- **source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz/check_request_utils.h**: `CheckRequestUtils` static utility class with `createHttpCheck()` and `createTcpCheck()` for building `CheckRequest` protobuf messages from request/connection context. Also defines `Matcher` interface and implementations (`HeaderKeyMatcher`, `NotHeaderKeyMatcher`) for header filtering.\n- **source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz/check_request_utils.cc**: Implementation of check request construction. Populates `AttributeContext` with peer info (`setAttrContextPeer()`), HTTP request details (`setHttpRequest()`), TLS session info (`setTLSSession()`), request body, and filtered headers.\n\n### Protobuf Definitions\n\n- **api/envoy/extensions/filters/http/ext_authz/v3/ext_authz.proto**: HTTP filter configuration: `ExtAuthz` message (main config with ~30 fields), `ExtAuthzPerRoute`, `CheckSettings`, `BufferSettings`, `HttpService`, `AuthorizationRequest`, `AuthorizationResponse`.\n- **api/envoy/extensions/filters/network/ext_authz/v3/ext_authz.proto**: Network filter configuration proto.\n- **api/envoy/service/auth/v3/external_auth.proto**: Authorization gRPC service definition (`Authorization` service with `Check` RPC), `CheckRequest`, `CheckResponse`, `OkHttpResponse`, `DeniedHttpResponse`.\n- **api/envoy/service/auth/v3/attribute_context.proto**: `AttributeContext` message with nested `Peer`, `Request`, `HttpRequest`, and `TLSSession` types that carry full request context to the authorization service.\n\n## 4. Failure Modes\n\n### Authorization Service Unavailable\n\nWhen the external authorization service is unreachable (network failure, DNS resolution failure, service crash):\n- **gRPC mode**: The gRPC async client fires `onFailure()` with a status like `Unavailable`, resulting in `CheckStatus::Error`.\n- **HTTP mode**: The HTTP async client fires `onFailure()` with a `Reset` reason, resulting in `CheckStatus::Error`.\n- **Behavior depends on `failure_mode_allow` configuration**:\n  - `failure_mode_allow: false` (default, fail-closed): Request is rejected with the configured `status_on_error` HTTP code (default 403). Response code detail: `ext_authz_error`. Stream flag: `UnauthorizedExternalService`.\n  - `failure_mode_allow: true` (fail-open): Request is allowed through. The `failure_mode_allowed` stat is incremented. If `failure_mode_allow_header_add` is true, the header `x-envoy-auth-failure-mode-allowed: true` is added to the upstream request so the backend knows authorization was not enforced.\n\n### Authorization Service Timeout\n\nWhen the authz service does not respond within the configured timeout:\n- **gRPC mode**: Results in a `DeadlineExceeded` gRPC status, which triggers `onFailure()` with `CheckStatus::Error`.\n- **HTTP mode**: The HTTP async client timeout triggers `onFailure()`, resulting in `CheckStatus::Error`.\n- The same `failure_mode_allow` logic applies as for service unavailability.\n\n### Authorization Explicitly Denied\n\nWhen the authorization service returns a denial:\n- **gRPC mode**: Any non-OK gRPC status in the `CheckResponse` results in `CheckStatus::Denied`. The response status code defaults to 403 but can be overridden by the `denied_response.status` field in the `CheckResponse`.\n- **HTTP mode**: Any non-200, non-5xx response from the authz service is treated as `CheckStatus::Denied`. The actual HTTP status code from the authz response is used as the denial status code.\n- The filter sends a local reply with the denial status code, the response body from the authz service (if any), and response headers specified in the authz response. Response code detail: `ext_authz_denied`. Stream flag: `UnauthorizedExternalService`.\n\n### Invalid Authorization Response\n\nWhen the authorization service returns a response with invalid header mutations or query parameter mutations (and `validate_mutations` is enabled):\n- The filter rejects the request with HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.\n- Response code detail: `ext_authz_invalid`.\n- The `invalid` stat counter is incremented.\n\n### HTTP Authorization Service Returns 5xx\n\nWhen the HTTP-based authorization service returns a 5xx status code:\n- Treated as `CheckStatus::Error` (not as a denial).\n- Same `failure_mode_allow` logic applies.\n\n### Authorization Cluster Not Found\n\nWhen the configured upstream cluster for the HTTP authz service does not exist:\n- The HTTP client logs `\"ext_authz cluster '{}' does not exist\"` at debug level.\n- Results in `CheckStatus::Error`.\n- Same `failure_mode_allow` logic applies.\n\n### Filter Disabled with deny_at_disable\n\nWhen the filter is disabled (via runtime flag or metadata matcher) and `deny_at_disable` is configured:\n- The request is rejected with `status_on_error` (default 403).\n- Response code detail: `ext_authz_error`.\n- The `disabled` stat counter is incremented.\n\n### Network Filter Failure\n\nFor the network (TCP) filter:\n- On `CheckStatus::Denied` or `CheckStatus::Error` (with `failure_mode_allow: false`): The connection is closed.\n- On `CheckStatus::Error` with `failure_mode_allow: true`: Data continues to flow.\n\n### Request Body Too Large\n\nWhen the request body exceeds `max_request_bytes` in `BufferSettings`:\n- If `allow_partial_message` is true, the check is sent with a truncated body and a flag indicating the body is partial.\n- If `allow_partial_message` is false, the check is sent once the buffer limit is hit, potentially with an incomplete body.\n\n## 5. A spike in `denied` may indicate a policy change or misconfiguration. The `invalid` counter indicates the authz service is returning malformed responses.\n\n### Logging\n\nThe filter uses Envoy's standard logging framework. Set the log level for `ext_authz` logger to see detailed output.\n\n**Key log messages (by level):**\n\n- **trace**: `\"Sending CheckRequest: {}\"` - Full serialized CheckRequest proto (in gRPC impl). `\"Received CheckResponse: {}\"` - Full serialized CheckResponse proto. Per-header mutation details (each header being set/added/appended/removed). `\"ext_authz filter calling authorization server\"` - Auth check initiation. `\"ext_authz filter allowed the request with error\"` - Fail-open triggered. `\"ext_authz filter rejected the request with an error\"` - Fail-closed triggered.\n- **debug**: `\"ext_authz cluster '{}' does not exist\"` - Authz cluster missing. `\"ext_authz filter is buffering the request\"` / `\"ext_authz filter finished buffering the request since {buffer is full | stream is ended}\"` - Body buffering lifecycle.\n\n**How to enable:** Set `--log-level ext_authz:trace` on the Envoy command line, or use the admin `/logging?ext_authz=trace` endpoint at runtime.\n\n### Distributed Tracing\n\nThe filter integrates with Envoy's tracing subsystem and adds tags to trace spans:\n\n| Trace Tag | Values | Meaning |\n|-----------|--------|---------|\n| `ext_authz_status` | `ext_authz_ok` or `ext_authz_unauthorized` | Authorization result |\n| `ext_authz_http_status` | HTTP status code string (e.g., `\"200\"`, `\"403\"`) | HTTP authz service response code (HTTP client only) |\n\nThe authorization check itself appears as a child span named `\"async <cluster_name> egress\"` under the parent request span. This lets you see authz latency in your tracing backend.\n\n### Response Code Details (Access Logs)\n\nThe filter sets `response_code_details` in stream info, which appears in access logs:\n\n| Detail String | Meaning |\n|---------------|---------|\n| `ext_authz_denied` | Request explicitly denied by authorization service |\n| `ext_authz_error` | Authorization service error (fail-closed) |\n| `ext_authz_invalid` | Invalid authorization response (bad mutations) |\n\nAdditionally, the `UnauthorizedExternalService` response flag is set for all denied/error responses, visible in access logs as the `%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` field (flag: `UAEX`).\n\n### Dynamic Metadata\n\nThe authz service can inject dynamic metadata into the request's stream info under the namespace `envoy.filters.http.ext_authz` (HTTP) or `envoy.filters.network.ext_authz` (network). This metadata is accessible in access log format strings via `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(envoy.filters.http.ext_authz:key)%`.\n\nThe filter automatically adds `ext_authz_duration` (in milliseconds) to dynamic metadata when the authorization check succeeds, providing a built-in latency measurement.\n\n### Filter State (ExtAuthzLoggingInfo)\n\nWhen `emit_filter_state_stats` is enabled, the HTTP filter stores an `ExtAuthzLoggingInfo` object in filter state containing:\n- `latency()` - Authorization check latency (microseconds)\n- `bytesSent()` - Bytes sent to authz service (gRPC only)\n- `bytesReceived()` - Bytes received from authz service (gRPC only)\n- `clusterInfo()` - Upstream authz cluster information\n- `upstreamHost()` - Specific upstream host used for the authz check\n\nThis data can be accessed by custom access log formatters or downstream filters for advanced observability.\n\n### Debugging Checklist\n\n1. **Check stats**: Look at `ext_authz.<prefix>.error` and `ext_authz.<prefix>.failure_mode_allowed` for service health issues.\n2. **Check access logs**: Look for `ext_authz_denied`, `ext_authz_error`, or `ext_authz_invalid` in `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` and `UAEX` in `%RESPONSE_FLAGS%`.\n3. **Enable trace logging**: Set `ext_authz:trace` to see full CheckRequest/CheckResponse payloads.\n4. **Check tracing**: Look for `ext_authz_status` span tags and the authz child span latency.\n5. **Verify cluster health**: Check the authz service cluster stats and health check status via Envoy admin (`/clusters`).\n6. **Check dynamic metadata**: Use `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(envoy.filters.http.ext_authz:ext_authz_duration)%` in access logs to monitor authz latency.\n7. **Verify configuration**: Ensure the authz cluster exists, timeouts are reasonable, and `failure_mode_allow` is set appropriately for your use case.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":126,"cache_read_input_tokens":39664,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":126},"output_tokens":25,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"bf44acc1-a45c-4fc6-b65c-5a9ac70e345e","uuid":"704f91bf-387c-40e6-a179-da6f76221322"}

Purpose\n\nThe ext_authz filter is an external authorization filter for Envoy proxy that delegates authorization decisions to an external service. Rather than embedding authorization logic directly in Envoy, it sends check requests to a separate authorization server and acts on the response (allow, deny, or error).\n\n**What problems does it solve?**\n\n- **Centralized authorization**: Decouples authorization logic from the proxy, allowing a single authorization service to enforce policies across an entire fleet of Envoy proxies.\n- **Fine-grained access control**: The authorization service receives rich request context (headers, path, client certificate, peer info, request body) and can make nuanced authorization decisions.\n- **Dynamic policy updates**: Authorization policies can be updated in the external service without redeploying Envoy.\n- **Protocol flexibility**: Supports both gRPC and HTTP protocols for communicating with the authorization service, enabling integration with a wide variety of auth backends (OPA, custom services, cloud IAM, etc.).\n\n**When would someone use it?**\n\n- Enforcing authentication/authorization at the edge or service mesh layer.\n- Implementing zero-trust networking where every request must be explicitly authorized.\n- Integrating with external policy engines (e.g., Open Policy Agent).\n- Adding authorization to services that lack their own auth implementation.\n\nThe filter operates at two layers:\n- **HTTP filter** (`envoy.filters.http.ext_authz`): Operates on HTTP requests with full access to headers, path, method, body, and can mutate request/response headers and query parameters based on the authorization response.\n- **Network filter** (`envoy.filters.network.ext_authz`): Operates at the TCP connection level, authorizing connections based on network attributes (source/destination addresses, TLS info) before any HTTP processing.\n\n## 2. Dependencies\n\n### Upstream Dependencies\n\n**Core Envoy Libraries:**\n- `source/common/http:codes_lib` / `envoy/http:codes_interface` - HTTP status code handling\n- `source/common/http:utility_lib` - HTTP utility functions\n- `source/common/http:headers_lib` - Header map manipulation\n- `source/common/http:async_client_lib` - HTTP async client for HTTP-mode authorization\n- `source/common/buffer:buffer_lib` - Request body buffering\n- `source/common/grpc:async_client_lib` / `source/common/grpc:typed_async_client_lib` - gRPC async client for gRPC-mode authorization\n- `source/common/router:config_lib` - Route configuration access\n- `source/common/runtime:runtime_protos_lib` - Runtime feature flags\n- `source/common/common:matchers_lib` - String/header matchers for filtering\n- `source/common/tracing:http_tracer_lib` - Distributed tracing integration\n- `source/common/network:utility_lib` - Network address utilities\n- `source/common/config:utility_lib` - Configuration parsing utilities\n- `source/common/protobuf:utility_lib` / `source/common/protobuf` - Protobuf support\n- `source/extensions/filters/common/mutation_rules:mutation_rules_lib` - Header mutation validation rules\n\n**Envoy Interfaces:**\n- `envoy/grpc:async_client_interface` / `envoy/grpc:async_client_manager_interface` - gRPC client abstractions\n- `envoy/http:filter_interface` - HTTP stream filter interface (`Http::StreamFilter`)\n- `envoy/http:header_map_interface` / `envoy/http:protocol_interface` - Header and protocol interfaces\n- `envoy/network:connection_interface` / `envoy/network:filter_interface` - Network filter interfaces (`Network::ReadFilter`)\n- `envoy/upstream:cluster_manager_interface` - Cluster manager for locating authz service clusters\n- `envoy/stats:stats_macros` - Statistics counter/gauge macros\n- `envoy/stream_info:stream_info_interface` - Per-stream metadata and info\n- `envoy/registry` - Extension registry for filter factory registration\n\n**Protobuf API Definitions:**\n- `@envoy_api//envoy/extensions/filters/http/ext_authz/v3:pkg_cc_proto` - HTTP filter configuration proto\n- `@envoy_api//envoy/extensions/filters/network/ext_authz/v3:pkg_cc_proto` - Network filter configuration proto\n- `@envoy_api//envoy/service/auth/v3:pkg_cc_proto` - Authorization service protocol (CheckRequest/CheckResponse)\n- `@envoy_api//envoy/config/core/v3:pkg_cc_proto` - `RawHttpClientImpl` for HTTP-based authz checks\n- `source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz:check_request_utils_lib` - `CheckRequestUtils` for building CheckRequest protos\n\n### Downstream Consumers\n\n**Filter Registration:**\nThe ext_authz filters are registered as named extensions in Envoy's filter chain system:\n- HTTP filter name: `envoy.filters.http.ext_authz` (registered in `source/extensions/extensions_build_config.bzl`)\n- Network filter name: `envoy.filters.network.ext_authz` (registered in `source/extensions/extensions_build_config.bzl`)\n\n**How it is configured in Envoy's filter chain:**\n- The HTTP variant is added to `http_filters` in an `HttpConnectionManager` listener filter configuration.\n- The Network variant is added to `filters` in a listener's `filter_chains` configuration.\n- Both support per-route configuration overrides via `ExtAuthzPerRoute` (HTTP) to disable or customize the filter on specific routes.\n\n**Security posture:** `robust_to_untrusted_downstream` (stable status).\n\n**Integration points:**\n- Any Envoy deployment can use ext_authz by configuring it in the filter chain and pointing it at an authorization service that implements the `envoy.service.auth.v3.Authorization` gRPC service or accepts HTTP check requests.\n- Downstream filters and access loggers can read dynamic metadata injected by ext_authz under the `envoy.filters.http.ext_authz` namespace.\n\n## 3. Relevant Components\n\n### HTTP Filter (`source/extensions/filters/http/ext_authz/`)\n\n- **source/extensions/filters/http/ext_authz/ext_authz.h**: Defines the core HTTP filter class `Filter` (extends `Http::StreamFilter`), configuration class `FilterConfig`, per-route configuration `FilterConfigPerRoute`, statistics struct `ExtAuthzFilterStats`, and `ExtAuthzLoggingInfo` for per-stream access log metadata. Contains the filter's state machine and callback interfaces.\n- **source/extensions/filters/http/ext_authz/ext_authz.cc**: Main HTTP filter implementation. Handles `decodeHeaders()` (initiates authz check), `decodeData()` (buffers request body), request body buffering, `onComplete()` callback (processes authorization response with OK/Denied/Error paths), header/query-parameter mutation, dynamic metadata injection, and `sendLocalReply()` for denied/error responses.\n- **source/extensions/filters/http/ext_authz/config.h**: Factory class `ExtAuthzFilterConfig` for creating HTTP ext_authz filter instances from protobuf configuration.\n- **source/extensions/filters/http/ext_authz/config.cc**: Configuration parsing and factory implementation. Creates either a gRPC or HTTP client based on configuration, sets up timeouts, and handles per-route configuration factories.\n\n### Network Filter (`source/extensions/filters/network/ext_authz/`)\n\n- **source/extensions/filters/network/ext_authz/ext_authz.h**: Defines the network filter class `Filter` (extends `Network::ReadFilter`), configuration class `Config`, and `InstanceStats` struct. Handles TCP-level authorization.\n- **source/extensions/filters/network/ext_authz/ext_authz.cc**: Network filter implementation. Handles `onNewConnection()` and `onData()` to trigger authorization checks, `onComplete()` callback for auth responses, connection close on denial/error, and dynamic metadata injection at the network layer.\n- **source/extensions/filters/network/ext_authz/config.h**: Factory class `ExtAuthzConfigFactory` for network filter instances.\n- **source/extensions/filters/network/ext_authz/config.cc**: Network filter configuration parsing and gRPC client creation.\n\n### Common/Shared Library (`source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz/`)\n\n- **source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz/ext_authz.h**: Defines the abstract `Client` interface (with `check()` and `cancel()` methods), `RequestCallbacks` interface, `Response` struct, `CheckStatus` enum (`OK`, `Denied`, `Error`), `ResponseCodeDetails` constants (`ext_authz_denied`, `ext_authz_error`, `ext_authz_invalid`), `TracingConstants`, and `HeaderValues` (e.g., `x-envoy-auth-failure-mode-allowed`).\n- **source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz/ext_authz_grpc_impl.h**: `GrpcClientImpl` class implementing the gRPC authorization client. Uses Envoy's typed async gRPC client to send `CheckRequest` messages to the `envoy.service.auth.v3.Authorization` service.\n- **source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz/ext_authz_grpc_impl.cc**: gRPC client implementation. Builds and sends CheckRequest, parses CheckResponse on `onSuccess()` (extracting header mutations, query parameter changes, dynamic metadata), handles `onFailure()` for gRPC errors. Helper functions for copying response mutations (`copyHeaderMutations`, `copyQueryParameterMutations`).\n- **source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz/ext_authz_http_impl.h**: `RawHttpClientImpl` class implementing the HTTP authorization client, and `ClientConfig` for HTTP-specific configuration (allowed headers, path prefix, matchers).\n- **source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz/ext_authz_http_impl.cc**: HTTP client implementation. Constructs HTTP requests to the authz service, sends via async HTTP client, parses responses in `toResponse()` (200 = OK, 5xx = Error, anything else = Denied), applies header matchers, extracts dynamic metadata from response headers.\n- **source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz/check_request_utils.h**: `CheckRequestUtils` static utility class with `createHttpCheck()` and `createTcpCheck()` for building `CheckRequest` protobuf messages from request/connection context. Also defines `Matcher` interface and implementations (`HeaderKeyMatcher`, `NotHeaderKeyMatcher`) for header filtering.\n- **source/extensions/filters/common/ext_authz/check_request_utils.cc**: Implementation of check request construction. Populates `AttributeContext` with peer info (`setAttrContextPeer()`), HTTP request details (`setHttpRequest()`), TLS session info (`setTLSSession()`), request body, and filtered headers.\n\n### Protobuf Definitions\n\n- **api/envoy/extensions/filters/http/ext_authz/v3/ext_authz.proto**: HTTP filter configuration: `ExtAuthz` message (main config with ~30 fields), `ExtAuthzPerRoute`, `CheckSettings`, `BufferSettings`, `HttpService`, `AuthorizationRequest`, `AuthorizationResponse`.\n- **api/envoy/extensions/filters/network/ext_authz/v3/ext_authz.proto**: Network filter configuration proto.\n- **api/envoy/service/auth/v3/external_auth.proto**: Authorization gRPC service definition (`Authorization` service with `Check` RPC), `CheckRequest`, `CheckResponse`, `OkHttpResponse`, `DeniedHttpResponse`.\n- **api/envoy/service/auth/v3/attribute_context.proto**: `AttributeContext` message with nested `Peer`, `Request`, `HttpRequest`, and `TLSSession` types that carry full request context to the authorization service.\n\n## 4. Failure Modes\n\n### Authorization Service Unavailable\n\nWhen the external authorization service is unreachable (network failure, DNS resolution failure, service crash):\n- **gRPC mode**: The gRPC async client fires `onFailure()` with a status like `Unavailable`, resulting in `CheckStatus::Error`.\n- **HTTP mode**: The HTTP async client fires `onFailure()` with a `Reset` reason, resulting in `CheckStatus::Error`.\n- **Behavior depends on `failure_mode_allow` configuration**:\n  - `failure_mode_allow: false` (default, fail-closed): Request is rejected with the configured `status_on_error` HTTP code (default 403). Response code detail: `ext_authz_error`. Stream flag: `UnauthorizedExternalService`.\n  - `failure_mode_allow: true` (fail-open): Request is allowed through. The `failure_mode_allowed` stat is incremented. If `failure_mode_allow_header_add` is true, the header `x-envoy-auth-failure-mode-allowed: true` is added to the upstream request so the backend knows authorization was not enforced.\n\n### Authorization Service Timeout\n\nWhen the authz service does not respond within the configured timeout:\n- **gRPC mode**: Results in a `DeadlineExceeded` gRPC status, which triggers `onFailure()` with `CheckStatus::Error`.\n- **HTTP mode**: The HTTP async client timeout triggers `onFailure()`, resulting in `CheckStatus::Error`.\n- The same `failure_mode_allow` logic applies as for service unavailability.\n\n### Authorization Explicitly Denied\n\nWhen the authorization service returns a denial:\n- **gRPC mode**: Any non-OK gRPC status in the `CheckResponse` results in `CheckStatus::Denied`. The response status code defaults to 403 but can be overridden by the `denied_response.status` field in the `CheckResponse`.\n- **HTTP mode**: Any non-200, non-5xx response from the authz service is treated as `CheckStatus::Denied`. The actual HTTP status code from the authz response is used as the denial status code.\n- The filter sends a local reply with the denial status code, the response body from the authz service (if any), and response headers specified in the authz response. Response code detail: `ext_authz_denied`. Stream flag: `UnauthorizedExternalService`.\n\n### Invalid Authorization Response\n\nWhen the authorization service returns a response with invalid header mutations or query parameter mutations (and `validate_mutations` is enabled):\n- The filter rejects the request with HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.\n- Response code detail: `ext_authz_invalid`.\n- The `invalid` stat counter is incremented.\n\n### HTTP Authorization Service Returns 5xx\n\nWhen the HTTP-based authorization service returns a 5xx status code:\n- Treated as `CheckStatus::Error` (not as a denial).\n- Same `failure_mode_allow` logic applies.\n\n### Authorization Cluster Not Found\n\nWhen the configured upstream cluster for the HTTP authz service does not exist:\n- The HTTP client logs `\"ext_authz cluster '{}' does not exist\"` at debug level.\n- Results in `CheckStatus::Error`.\n- Same `failure_mode_allow` logic applies.\n\n### Filter Disabled with deny_at_disable\n\nWhen the filter is disabled (via runtime flag or metadata matcher) and `deny_at_disable` is configured:\n- The request is rejected with `status_on_error` (default 403).\n- Response code detail: `ext_authz_error`.\n- The `disabled` stat counter is incremented.\n\n### Network Filter Failure\n\nFor the network (TCP) filter:\n- On `CheckStatus::Denied` or `CheckStatus::Error` (with `failure_mode_allow: false`): The connection is closed.\n- On `CheckStatus::Error` with `failure_mode_allow: true`: Data continues to flow.\n\n### Request Body Too Large\n\nWhen the request body exceeds `max_request_bytes` in `BufferSettings`:\n- If `allow_partial_message` is true, the check is sent with a truncated body and a flag indicating the body is partial.\n- If `allow_partial_message` is false, the check is sent once the buffer limit is hit, potentially with an incomplete body.\n\n## 5. Testing\n\n### Unit Tests\n\n**HTTP Filter Unit Tests:**\n- **test/extensions/filters/http/ext_authz/ext_authz_test.cc**: 80+ test cases covering the full HTTP filter behavior. Test fixture: `HttpFilterTest` / `HttpFilterTestParam`. Covers: configuration merging, stats collection, error handling (fail-close, fail-open, custom status codes), request data buffering, header-only requests, WebSocket/HTTP2 upgrades, route-based configuration, header manipulation (add/append/remove/set), dynamic metadata ingestion, query parameter mutations, response header handling, filter enable/disable, deny-at-disable, and header mutation rule validation.\n\n**HTTP Filter Config Tests:**\n- **test/extensions/filters/http/ext_authz/config_test.cc**: Factory and configuration validation tests. Debugging\n\n### Statistics (Metrics)\n\nAll ext_authz stats are prefixed with `ext_authz.<stat_prefix>.` where `stat_prefix` is configured in the filter config.\n\n**HTTP filter counters:**\n| Stat Name | Meaning |\n|-----------|---------|\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.ok` | Requests authorized successfully |\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.denied` | Requests explicitly denied by authz service |\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.error` | Authorization service errors (timeout, unavailable, 5xx) |\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.disabled` | Requests where the filter was disabled |\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.failure_mode_allowed` | Errors allowed through due to `failure_mode_allow: true` |\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.invalid` | Invalid authorization responses (bad header mutations) |\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.ignored_dynamic_metadata` | Dynamic metadata ignored (ingestion disabled) |\n\n**Network filter counters:**\n| Stat Name | Meaning |\n|-----------|---------|\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.total` | Total authorization checks |\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.ok` | Authorized connections |\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.denied` | Denied connections |\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.error` | Authorization errors |\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.disabled` | Disabled filter invocations |\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.cx_closed` | Connections closed due to authz failure |\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.failure_mode_allowed` | Errors allowed through |\n\n**Network filter gauge:**\n| Stat Name | Meaning |\n|-----------|---------|\n| `ext_authz.<prefix>.active` | Currently in-flight authorization checks |\n\n**Cluster-scoped stats** (when `charge_cluster_response_stats` is enabled): `ext_authz_ok_`, `ext_authz_denied_`, `ext_authz_error_`, `ext_authz_invalid_`, `ext_authz_failure_mode_allowed_` are charged to the upstream authz cluster stats.\n\n**What to check first:** A sudden spike in `error` or `failure_mode_allowed` indicates the authorization service is unhealthy. A spike in `denied` may indicate a policy change or misconfiguration. The `invalid` counter indicates the authz service is returning malformed responses.\n\n### Logging\n\nThe filter uses Envoy's standard logging framework. Set the log level for `ext_authz` logger to see detailed output.\n\n**Key log messages (by level):**\n\n- **trace**: `\"Sending CheckRequest: {}\"` - Full serialized CheckRequest proto (in gRPC impl). `\"Received CheckResponse: {}\"` - Full serialized CheckResponse proto. Per-header mutation details (each header being set/added/appended/removed). `\"ext_authz filter calling authorization server\"` - Auth check initiation. `\"ext_authz filter allowed the request with error\"` - Fail-open triggered. `\"ext_authz filter rejected the request with an error\"` - Fail-closed triggered.\n- **debug**: `\"ext_authz cluster '{}' does not exist\"` - Authz cluster missing. `\"ext_authz filter is buffering the request\"` / `\"ext_authz filter finished buffering the request since {buffer is full | stream is ended}\"` - Body buffering lifecycle.\n\n**How to enable:** Set `--log-level ext_authz:trace` on the Envoy command line, or use the admin `/logging?ext_authz=trace` endpoint at runtime.\n\n### Distributed Tracing\n\nThe filter integrates with Envoy's tracing subsystem and adds tags to trace spans:\n\n| Trace Tag | Values | Meaning |\n|-----------|--------|---------|\n| `ext_authz_status` | `ext_authz_ok` or `ext_authz_unauthorized` | Authorization result |\n| `ext_authz_http_status` | HTTP status code string (e.g., `\"200\"`, `\"403\"`) | HTTP authz service response code (HTTP client only) |\n\nThe authorization check itself appears as a child span named `\"async <cluster_name> egress\"` under the parent request span. This lets you see authz latency in your tracing backend.\n\n### Response Code Details (Access Logs)\n\nThe filter sets `response_code_details` in stream info, which appears in access logs:\n\n| Detail String | Meaning |\n|---------------|---------|\n| `ext_authz_denied` | Request explicitly denied by authorization service |\n| `ext_authz_error` | Authorization service error (fail-closed) |\n| `ext_authz_invalid` | Invalid authorization response (bad mutations) |\n\nAdditionally, the `UnauthorizedExternalService` response flag is set for all denied/error responses, visible in access logs as the `%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` field (flag: `UAEX`).\n\n### Dynamic Metadata\n\nThe authz service can inject dynamic metadata into the request's stream info under the namespace `envoy.filters.http.ext_authz` (HTTP) or `envoy.filters.network.ext_authz` (network). This metadata is accessible in access log format strings via `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(envoy.filters.http.ext_authz:key)%`.\n\nThe filter automatically adds `ext_authz_duration` (in milliseconds) to dynamic metadata when the authorization check succeeds, providing a built-in latency measurement.\n\n### Filter State (ExtAuthzLoggingInfo)\n\nWhen `emit_filter_state_stats` is enabled, the HTTP filter stores an `ExtAuthzLoggingInfo` object in filter state containing:\n- `latency()` - Authorization check latency (microseconds)\n- `bytesSent()` - Bytes sent to authz service (gRPC only)\n- `bytesReceived()` - Bytes received from authz service (gRPC only)\n- `clusterInfo()` - Upstream authz cluster information\n- `upstreamHost()` - Specific upstream host used for the authz check\n\nThis data can be accessed by custom access log formatters or downstream filters for advanced observability.\n\n### Debugging Checklist\n\n1. **Check stats**: Look at `ext_authz.<prefix>.error` and `ext_authz.<prefix>.failure_mode_allowed` for service health issues.\n2. **Check access logs**: Look for `ext_authz_denied`, `ext_authz_error`, or `ext_authz_invalid` in `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` and `UAEX` in `%RESPONSE_FLAGS%`.\n3. **Enable trace logging**: Set `ext_authz:trace` to see full CheckRequest/CheckResponse payloads.\n4. **Check tracing**: Look for `ext_authz_status` span tags and the authz child span latency.\n5. **Verify cluster health**: Check the authz service cluster stats and health check status via Envoy admin (`/clusters`).\n6. **Check dynamic metadata**: Use `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(envoy.filters.http.ext_authz:ext_authz_duration)%` in access logs to monitor authz latency.\n7. **Verify configuration**: Ensure the authz cluster exists, timeouts are reasonable, and `failure_mode_allow` is set appropriately for your use case.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}
